US spot Bitcoin ETFs see $999M net inflows, Ether ETFs add $270M U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $999 million in net inflows on Sept. 21, according to SoSoValue, led by BlackRock’s IBIT with $381 million. Spot Ether ETFs added another $270 million, with BlackRock’s ETHA attracting $110 million. — link

Highlight Clip: Coinbase CEO Responds to Stablecoin Rewards and Banking Regulation Debate Coinbase CEO Responds to Stablecoin Rewards and Banking Regulation Debate Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong addressed questions about how USDC rewards differ from bank interest and whether Coinbase should face bank capital and liquidity requirements in a September 19 interview with MoneyRehabPodcast. Armstrong said the rewards pass on part of the returns from underlying short-term U.S. Treasuries and are legally distinguished from deposit interest. He emphasized that Coinbase does not issue stablecoins or engage in fractional-reserve lending, while stablecoin issuers maintain full reserves. He also criticized some major banks for allegedly using government intervention to restrict competition. — link

Ethena’s USDe Briefly Plunges to $0.92 on Binance Before Rapid Recovery Ethena’s synthetic dollar USDe briefly fell as low as 0.9202 USDT on Binance’s USDE/USDT spot pair at around 1 p.m. on Sept. 22 before quickly recovering to about 0.9996 USDT. The move came shortly before Binance began a scheduled infrastructure wallet upgrade at 2 p.m., during which deposits and withdrawals across all networks were suspended for about an hour, while a broader system-maintenance window runs through 5 p.m.; spot and futures trading remain unaffected. There is currently no evidence linking the USDe price dislocation to Binance’s maintenance. — link

Upbit Flags SOPH for Review as Binance Drops Seven USDC Spot Pairs South Korea’s largest crypto exchange Upbit designated Sophon (SOPH) as a trading-warning asset and suspended deposits, citing concerns over disclosure, token-circulation plan changes and the transparency of related procedures; the review could ultimately lead to delisting if issues are not resolved. Meanwhile, Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by trading volume, will remove seven USDC spot pairs — AIXBT, DOLO, ENJ, HUMA, SXT, TNSR and TURTLE — on Sept. 25, citing liquidity and trading-volume considerations, while the underlying tokens will remain listed through other pairs. — link
